title: Daily Executive Brief — Calendar × Salesforce × Meeting History

sections.label: 1 · MORNING SWEEP
sections.note: Runs before you're at your desk. Today's calendar is pulled once and each meeting handled individually, so one unreachable record never costs you the whole brief.

sections.label: 2 · GATHER CONTEXT
sections.note: Per meeting: the Salesforce account and open opportunity, plus the last real interaction recalled from your meeting history — what was said, what was promised, what is still outstanding.

sections.label: 3 · PREP EACH MEETING
sections.note: A brief per meeting: where the deal stands, the open action items with owners, recommended talking points, and the next step to push for. The prep you would do at 11pm the night before, done at 6am by something that never skips it.

sections.label: 4 · PRIORITISE
sections.note: Once every meeting is prepped, the day is ranked as a whole — deal stage, deadline pressure, overdue follow-ups, and how much preparation each one actually needs. Ranking requires seeing all of them at once, which is why it happens after the loop, not inside it.

sections.label: 5 · DELIVER
sections.note: A structured agenda with time allocations lands in your inbox before the first meeting, with the three things that actually matter today pushed to Slack for the phone-in-the-car read.

nodes.label: Recall Last Interaction
nodes.notes: Searches past meeting notes and threads for this account

nodes.label: Build Meeting Brief
nodes.notes: Open items · talking points · next step

output_sample.day_summary: Two of six meetings actually decide anything today. Halvorsen is the day — legal joined the invite, which they have not done before, and the renewal closes in 11 days with a security review still open. Everything else can run on autopilot.

top_priority.why_first: Legal added to the invite for the first time; $148k renewal closes in 11 days; security questionnaire outstanding 9 days
top_priority.last_interaction: 17 Jul — Paul asked for SOC 2 report and pricing on the extra 40 seats. You sent pricing on the 18th. The SOC 2 was never sent.

open_action_items.item: Confirm 40-seat expansion pricing holds through Q3

talking_points: Lead with the SOC 2 — it is the only thing you owe them and legal being on the call means it is now the blocker
The 40-seat expansion is still unconfirmed; getting it into this renewal is worth $31k over doing it separately later
They have been in Negotiation 22 days against a 14-day average — name the timeline directly
top_priority.recommended_next_step: Ask for a signature target date on the call, not after it

deprioritised: Weekly marketing sync — no decisions pending, forward notes instead
